chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who says to the jeweller, 'Make this ring for me, and I will exchange for you a fresh dirham for a worn dirham.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a jeweller by exchanging old coins for new ones?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that swapping a fresh dirham for a worn one as payment for a goldsmith's service is permissible, distinguishing it from *riba al-fadl* by treating the currency exchange as incidental to the service contract (*ijarah*). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that minor disparities in coin condition do not invalidate transactions when coupled with a legitimate service, reflecting the practical flexibility of early Islamic commercial law.
